fatal_errors: The cited evidence concerns intrinsic CO oxidation by high-entropy spinel oxides and does not establish that such oxides can stabilize isolated platinum-group-metal sites, permit lower PGM loading, or improve PGM-catalyst durability.
The proposed dry, lean CO-only regime omits the water-containing cyclic lean/rich ageing and near-stoichiometric NO/CO/hydrocarbon feed central to the target automotive-catalyst problem.

The claimed approximately 60% reduction in light-off temperature is imported from a comparison of 7-metal and 4-metal spinel oxides, not from reduced-PGM catalysts, and percentage reductions in Celsius temperature are physically misleading.

The experiment changes support composition, PGM loading, and likely PGM dispersion simultaneously, so it cannot determine whether any performance difference arises from configurational entropy or simply from loading and dispersion differences.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the broad objective of improving automotive-catalyst activity and durability while reducing PGM use, and it supplies useful boundaries and a nominal falsification rule. However, it does not reconstruct the hidden intervention, which was a closed-loop high-throughput and machine-learning-guided search over multielement alloy compositions and solvothermal processing conditions evaluated after severe ageing. Its proposed mechanism—entropy-enhanced vacancies stabilizing isolated PGM atoms—is also unrelated to the target's ageing-induced Cu–Pt electronic reconstruction and alloy/support interfacial effects. Most importantly, E1 supports improved dry lean CO oxidation by a 7-metal spinel itself; it does not support the crucial extension to a low-loading PGM-on-spinel catalyst. A stronger test would compare entropy-varied supports at identical PGM identity, loading, and initial dispersion, include a reduced-loading conventional-support control, apply realistic wet cyclic lean/rich ageing, and measure species-resolved NO, CO, and hydrocarbon light-off after ageing.
